content.punchline: Within-ecotype, within-substudy meta-analysis surfaces six actionable pathobionts that replicate at 88% on a held-out cohort

slides.speaker_notes_seed: S2 opens the target-discovery argument. The key insight this substory delivers: stratifying by ecotype before running differential abundance eliminates the CMD cohort-confound that was reversing effect signs in the naive analysis. Once the design is clean, six pathobionts rise clearly above the scoring threshold — and the E1 set is externally validated on HMP2, a genuinely held-out cohort never seen in training. The E3 set is honest about its single-study provenance. Transition cue: these six targets are the input package for Pillar 4 phage-availability scoring in S3.

content.title: Confound-free design: within-ecotype × within-substudy meta-analysis eliminates CMD cohort bias

Filter: IBD substudies
with ≥10 CD + nonIBD

step_caption: Ecotype labels partition samples before any DA — no self-referential leakage
Only substudies containing both CD and nonIBD are eligible (4 of 51 CMD studies)
CLR-Δ meta-analysed within-substudy per ecotype; zero study-level confound

slides.speaker_notes_seed: REPORT §5a explains why this design is necessary: CMD pools 51 source studies but zero sub-studies contain both HC and CD. The standard CD-vs-HC LME with substudy random effect is structurally unidentifiable (statsmodels mixedlm silently fails to converge). The fix is CD-vs-nonIBD within IBD sub-studies — four CMD studies qualify: HallAB_2017 (89 CD/73 nonIBD), LiJ_2014 (76/10), IjazUZ_2017 (56/38), NielsenHB_2014 (21/248). Feature leakage is avoided because clustering axis and DA axis are disjoint. Key caveat to surface: E1 is meta-viable across two sub-studies (82 CD/280 nonIBD); E3 is single-study only (22 CD/31 nonIBD in HallAB_2017). This asymmetry drives the STRONG vs provisional verdict in the next slide.

slides.speaker_notes_seed: Numbers are from REPORT §5g NB05 scoring table. Four criteria scored (A3 literature+cohort CD-association 0–5; A4 protective-analog exclusion pass/fail; A5 engraftment/strain-adaptation 0–1; A6 BGC inflammatory mediator 0–1). The engraftment pathobionts (H. hathewayi, M. gnavus, E. coli, E. lenta, E. bolteae) dominate because they carry A5=1.0 by construction — these are the donor-2708 transfer species confirmed in NB04c. F. plautii earns A5=0.5 via Kumbhari strain-competition evidence. Tier-B candidates (score 2.2–2.4, e.g., E. asparagiformis, S. salivarius) are held back; phage-availability scoring in Pillar 4 can promote them. Score total = 4.0 + 3.8 + 3.6 + 3.3 + 3.3 + 2.8 — all verbatim from REPORT §5g table.

content.subtitle: E1 Tier-A sign-concordance on independently held-out HMP2 cohort
content.sub_pointer: 45 of 51 E1 Tier-A candidates are CD-enriched in both discovery (cMD) and HMP2
content.source_footer: REPORT.md §5f (NB04h); HMP2 n=593 CD / 337 nonIBD projected-E1 samples

slides.speaker_notes_seed: Number is verbatim from REPORT §5f: '45/51 (88.2%) are sign-concordant (both CD↑)' in the HMP2 projected-E1 subset. HMP2 is a genuinely held-out cohort — HMP_2019_ibdmdb was absent from the CMD_IBD training-set substudy list; same MetaPhlAn3 pipeline as training data so no Kaiju fragility. Projection confidence is high: median max LDA posterior 0.861, 80.4% of samples above 0.70 threshold. Two of the top 20 fail: S. thermophilus (sign-discordant — HMP2 E1 effect slightly negative, likely differential dairy exposure) and B. stercoris (sign-discordant, n.s.). These 6 non-concordant species are sub-threshold Tier-B candidates, not the 6 actionable Tier-A. Transition: with E1 confirmed externally, the contrast with E3's provisional status (next slide) is stark and honest.

content.title: E3 Tier-A is preliminary evidence only; all six targets cluster in a single co-occurrence module per ecotype
bullets: E3 Tier-A (40 candidates) rests on single study HallAB_2017 (22 CD / 31 nonIBD); HMP2 has only 10 E3 subjects — insufficient for E3 replication (31% of UC Davis patients inherit this provisional status)
4–5 of the 6 actionable Tier-A targets co-cluster in one pathobiont module per ecotype subnet (E1_all, E1_CD, E3_all, E3_CD subnets tested; CLR-Spearman |ρ| > 0.3, Louvain community detection)
Single-module co-occurrence supports multi-target cocktail design: targets share ecological conditions, hitting 3+ simultaneously may compound effects

slides.speaker_notes_seed: Two distinct analyses on one slide — need clear denominator labelling. E3 provisional framing from REPORT §5c: 'The E3 list should be treated as provisional until a second cMD-IBD sub-study that populates E3 with ≥10 CD and ≥10 nonIBD samples becomes available.' This is A6 (strength ⚠ partial) — language must not say 'validates' or 'demonstrates.' The co-occurrence finding is A7 (strength ✓ direct): REPORT §5h NB06 H2d verdict: 'in every subnet, a single module contains 4-5 of the 6 actionable Tier-A candidates.' Module sizes: E1_all module 1 = 84 nodes; E1_CD module 0 = 75 nodes; E3_all module 1 = 76 nodes; E3_CD module 1 = 57 nodes. Note: H2d verdict is formally 'PARTIAL' because raw mean-actionable-per-module (1.38) falls below the ≥2 plan bar — but the signal is concentrated in one module per subnet, which is the biological interpretation that matters for the cocktail-design argument. Surface the nominal-PARTIAL caveat in delivery.
